newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil spill more than 60,000 barrels -Navy.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil spill more than 60,000 barrels -Navy.

text.p: The Venezuelan Navy said on Monday that more than 60,000 barrels of heavy crude oil was spilled by a Greek-flagged tanker that ran aground near the Caribbean coast on Friday.
In a press statement, the Navy said it was helping state oil company PDVSA to control the spill, which threatens to pollute coastline in the Falcon and Zulia states in the northwest of the country.
The spills is one of the worst in Venezuela in recent years and could take at least a month to clean up.
The Nissos Amorgos tanker was carrying 474,000 barrels of heavy crude from Lake Maracaibo to the Gela terminal in Italy.
Originally, Venezuela's state oil subsidiary Maraven, which chartered the vessel, said 24,000 barrels were spilled when the ship grounded in the Lake Maracaibo shipping lane.

When the first spill was contained, the Maracaibo harbour master authorised the ship to Cardon about 93 miles (150 kilometres) to the east, the Navy said. The tanker was then intercepted by the coastal patrol vessel and an inspection revealed an oil slick behind the vessel.
The slick restricted fishing and recreation in the area, the Navy said.
